summary: Round-4 independent arbitration of the 66-case Python EC inventory at source digest sha256:476bc41d. All six axes were re-earned against this digest rather than carried over from the round-3 record. The round-3 blocking finding is closed and I re-derived the proof with my own harness instead of reading the author's: in the wi-remove-agent-estimate-spec-check branch of src/migration_clusters/work_item_planning.py the legacy work item's ready-lane placement is now asserted directly, and dropping ('Legacy estimate fixture', 'ready_now') from planning_lanes moves from 0/10 rejections to 3/10, including the claiming case itself. I added two variants the author did not name - the legacy lane moved to 'blocked' and to 'ready_later' - and both are rejected 3/10, so the assertion pins ready-lane membership rather than mere presence. A full 14-field mutation sweep with subtractive mutators now leaves no observable undetected: legacy_slug went 0/10 to 2/10, and the three remaining MISS entries in my output are harness artifacts, not gaps - bounded_labels losing 'priority:p1' or 'type:change' is covered by the dedicated wi-typed-priority-label case and by the bounded_type assertion, both outside the snapshot path my harness stubs, and planning_estimate_tokens 'emptied' is a degenerate no-op because the baseline is already the empty tuple. My unmutated control produced 0 rejections, confirming no false failure was introduced (my script labels that row MISS by construction, since for the control zero is the correct result). The two beyond-prescription changes were attacked specifically and both hold. The two-label return is a genuine improvement and breaks no evidence consumer: runner.py accepts any non-empty list of non-empty strings, inventory_parity.py line 83 asserts only that ASSERTIONS is non-empty and never binds it to the returned list, the stability path compares returned lists across attempts and these are literals so the comparison stays deterministic, and the persisted evidence file now records assertion_count 2 with both clauses stated, so the under-claim I flagged in round 3 is resolved. On the legacy_slug literal I am upholding the author's judgement while disagreeing with its placement, and this is recorded as a non-blocking observation rather than a finding. It is not tautological - legacy_slug is read back from aw wi create output, so pinning it does test aw's title-to-slug derivation - and it is not a false-green risk; the cost is brittleness, and the assertion sits in _planning_expectations where it binds a derivation rule that neither operational case's promise names. Blocking on it would also be inconsistent of me, because the fixture titles are already inline literals at six sites in this module including the lane assertions I myself prescribed, so the coupling class predates this change. The shape I would prefer: hoist 'Bounded planning fixture' and 'Legacy estimate fixture' to module-level constants and derive the expected slug from the legacy title constant, so a fixture rename moves both sides at once and the existing six-site duplication is cleaned in the same pass; alternatively move a literal slug-derivation assertion into a case that actually claims slug derivation and assert only distinct non-empty identity here. Execution and fail-closed behavior were fully re-measured at this digest, not inherited: a reviewer-owned sweep executing each case's canonical command verbatim from pyproject.toml passed 66/66 with zero failures, and the empty-implementation control again turns 62/66 red under an exit-0 no-output aw binary, with the 4 that bypass run_aw also red once their own subjects are stubbed - so 66/66 fail closed on an empty implementation. The three cases the new assertions touch were re-run repeatedly with no flake. Structural gates re-run green at this digest: inventory_parity.py self-consistent at 66 cases / 74 retained Rust invariants / dimensions behavior 50, efficiency 8, stability 8; claim_reconciliation.py --verify status clean with rust_invariant_case_count 0; all five migration_reconciliation.py verify modes green including --guidance and --projections; aw ec check clean with expected_case_count == case_count == 66 and stale false; aw ec lock --check clean at 90 sources and 66 cases. I re-derived claim binding and dimension coverage independently: exactly 14 unbound use_case_ids, every one an '-operational-' id that inventory_parity.py lines 93-97 positively requires to be case-local, zero non-operational unbound ids, zero capabilities missing a CapabilityType-required dimension, and zero declared dimensions without a case. Oracle independence is unchanged and re-verified by spot-checking the round-3 invariants in every other touched surface: td_terminal.py still proves wrapper teardown by os.kill liveness and pins failure_kind single_flight and the exact launches ledger, capability_manual.py still carries the 'Python EC scaffold is incomplete' guard, project_local_gates.py still asserts clean False with 'executed 0 tests', and wi_contract_fixture.py run_aw retains its expect_success semantics. Two disclosures the human auditor should weigh. First, I could not confirm the author's statement that the change was confined to work_item_planning.py: every file under external-contracts/src has an mtime later than my round-3 submission, and mtime is not content, so rather than trust the confinement claim I re-verified all six axes from scratch at this digest - the acceptance rests on that re-verification, not on the confinement claim. Second, aw ec lock --check reports locked_source_digest sha256:70b330f0, a different value from this review digest; those are separate digest domains (the lock spans 90 sources) and the lock reports clean, so this is expected rather than a defect. The author's correction to a statement we both made is verified and correct: sha256:302da1f6 is the canonical-JSON digest from _manifest_digest() at migration_reconciliation.py lines 58-60, not the raw file hash, which is 58a588ee85c1ea7b82474ce87c14301ee5f7bee8c13b4c395f4ae90b4053a942; the manifest is byte-identical to HEAD by git diff --quiet. Still outside EC scope and still open for the parent: the gate declared at CAPABILITIES.md line 312 (migration_reconciliation.py verify --baseline --batch-plan) remains red, is pre-existing, and is bound by no EC case. This record is agent-backed arbitration input for the human batch audit, not human acceptance evidence, and it authorizes only source digest sha256:476bc41d.
